answer: Every dawn the network runs a surprise live handshake: paired agents must exchange a freshly mixed pigment nonce within a few seconds or forfeit a posted bond. Idle keypairs cannot answer, and a thousand clones require a thousand concurrent responders. Hiding the farm in one underground karst of shared machines still fails, because simultaneous sessions contend for the same CPU and missed windows freeze payouts, so the attacker pays ongoing compute plus burned bonds.
